# Quick Study Guide: 4. Document Retrieval & Query Architecture (CRUD Read)

> "find(query, projection) retrieves all documents in a collection that match a given query filter, returning a cursor. Calling find() with no arguments returns every document in the collection. findOne(query, projection) retrieves the first document that matches a given query filter, returning a single document (or null) instead of a cursor."

## 1. Topic Executive Overview

This advanced systems revision sheet distills the high-yield architectural invariants of **4. Document Retrieval & Query Architecture (CRUD Read)**, covering wire protocol commands, WiredTiger storage behavior, B-tree index impact, and edge-case failure modes.

## 4.1 Cursor-Based Querying (find())

> "find(query, projection) retrieves all documents in a collection that match a given query filter, returning a cursor. Calling find() with no arguments returns every document in the collection."

- **L-3.1 Unfiltered (`COLLSCAN`) vs. Equality-Filtered (`IXSCAN`) Retrieval.** Calling `find()` or `find({})` executes a full collection scan (`COLLSCAN`) across all WiredTiger data pages. Passing an equality predicate `{ age: 18 }` (or `{ grade: 8 }`) allows the query planner to select a B-tree index scan (`IXSCAN`) if an index covers the predicate field.
- **L-3.2 Lazy Cursor State Machine, `firstBatch` / `getMore` & Modifier Chaining.** Because `find()` evaluates lazily, chaining `.sort()`, `.skip()`, and `.limit()` mutates the client-side `Cursor` specification in memory before any network packet is sent. When drained, `mongod` returns an initial `firstBatch` (default 101 docs or 16 MB) along with a 64-bit `cursorId` for subsequent `{ getMore }` batch fetches (`mongosh` displays 20 docs per interactive page).

```javascript
// 1. Construct lazy Cursor with equality predicate and projection
const cursor = db.students.find({ age: 18 }, { name: 1, grade: 1, _id: 0 })
  .sort({ name: 1 })
  .skip(0)
  .limit(10);

// 2. Inspect query execution plan (COLLSCAN vs IXSCAN)
db.students.find({ age: 18 }).explain("executionStats");
```

| Cursor Property / Stage | `mongosh` Interactive Behavior | Driver / Wire Protocol Behavior |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Return Object | `Cursor` (auto-prints first 20 docs) | Unevaluated `FindCursor` iterator |
| Initial Wire Batch (`firstBatch`) | Drains 20 docs; prompts `Type "it"` | Up to `101` documents (or `16 MB`) |
| Subsequent Batches (`getMore`) | Triggered by typing `it` | Dispatches `{ getMore: cursorId, collection }` |
| Unmatched Filter (`0` hits) | Prints nothing (empty cursor) | `cursor.hasNext()` returns `false` |

---

## 4.2 Single Document Lookup (findOne())

> "findOne(query, projection) retrieves the first document that matches a given query filter, returning a single document (or null) instead of a cursor."

- **L-3.1 Command Syntax, Predicate Filtering & Second-Argument BSON Projection.** `findOne(query, projection)` supports the full predicate AST in its first parameter (`{ age: { $gte: 18 } }`) and BSON field projection masking (`{ name: 1, _id: 0 }`) in its second parameter, executing with `limit: 1` and `singleBatch: true`.
- **L-3.2 Eager Unwrapping (`Object | null`) & Runtime `TypeError` on Cursor Chaining.** Because the client driver unwraps `cursor.firstBatch[0]` (returning `null` if `firstBatch` is empty) before returning to the caller, the return value is a plain deserialized BSON object or `null`—never a `Cursor` instance. Invoking `.sort()`, `.skip()`, or `.limit()` on `findOne()` is therefore syntactically invalid.

```javascript
// 1. Eager single-document lookup with range predicate and projection
const doc = db.students.findOne(
  { age: { $gte: 18 } },
  { name: 1, _id: 0 }
);
// Wire RPC: { find: "students", filter: { age: { $gte: 18 } }, projection: { name: 1, _id: 0 }, limit: 1, singleBatch: true }
// Returns: { name: "Aditi" } (or null if 0 documents match)

// 2. Workaround if you need sorted single-document lookup:
db.students.find({ age: { $gte: 18 } }).sort({ age: -1 }).limit(1);
```

| Execution Attribute | `find(query, projection)` | `findOne(query, projection)` |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Evaluation Model | Lazy `Cursor` builder | Eager execution & batch unwrapping |
| Wire Protocol Flags | Standard batching (`firstBatch` + `getMore`) | `limit: 1, singleBatch: true` |
| Server Scan Termination | Scans all matches (unless `.limit()` chained) | Short-circuits immediately at 1st match |
| Post-Call Method Chaining | Fluent `Cursor` pipeline methods | Prohibited (`Object` or `null` returned) |

---

## Rapid Exam Trap Checklist

- **Architectural Invariant 1 — Lazy vs. Eager Evaluation**: `find()` constructs a lazy client-side `Cursor` descriptor that only dispatches `{ find }` when iterated, whereas `findOne()` executes eagerly with `limit: 1, singleBatch: true`.
- **Architectural Invariant 2 — `mongosh` Batch Draining**: By default, `mongosh` drains the first 20 documents of a `find()` cursor and prompts `Type "it" for more`, whereas drivers iterate across `firstBatch` and `getMore` buffers.
- **Architectural Invariant 3 — `COLLSCAN` vs. `IXSCAN`**: Calling `find({})` forces a full collection scan (`COLLSCAN`), whereas equality predicates like `find({ age: 18 })` can utilize a B-tree index scan (`IXSCAN`) if indexed.
